Summary of what I did
- Listed available automation skills.
- Searched available tools for Salesforce/Gmail actions.
- Attempted to locate the VP of Sales renewal-policy message and contracts expiring in the next 30 days via the Salesforce connector:
  - Tried querying EmailMessage and User for vp.sales@company.com — EmailMessage object not available and no matching User found.
  - Tried querying Contract object — Contract object not accessible via this connector.
  - Searched Document/Note for "Renewal Policy" — no matching records.
  - Queried Opportunity for Renewal-type opportunities — query returned no results or was rejected (some SOQL constructs not supported by the connector).
- No emails were sent and no Salesforce records were updated because I could not retrieve the required records.

Why I couldn’t finish
- The Salesforce connector exposed here supports a limited set of object types and a restricted SOQL parser. Contract and EmailMessage objects (and some SOQL date functions) are not accessible in this environment, so I couldn’t:
  - Find contracts with EndDate in the next 30 days.
  - Retrieve the VP of Sales renewal policy email from Salesforce.
  - Identify qualifying accounts or related opportunities to update/send emails.

Recommended next steps (I can proceed as soon as you choose one)
1) Provide the renewal policy content or the VP of Sales email (forward or paste the pricing and account-standing criteria here).
   - I will use those criteria to identify qualifying accounts and generate/send renewal agreements and create flags/tasks for review.

2) Provide a list (CSV or sheet) of contracts/accounts expiring in the next 30 days (ContractNumber, AccountId/Name, Primary contact email, Payment status, Outstanding balance, OpportunityId if available).
   - I will send renewal agreements to qualifying accounts, flag the rest, and update the related opportunities.

3) Grant connector access to the Contract and EmailMessage objects (or allow broader SOQL queries).
   - I will run automated queries to find expiring contracts, apply the VP policy, email qualifying accounts from Salesforce, flag non-qualifiers with tasks/notes, and update Opportunity records (e.g., set stage to Contract Sent, add next step).

If you prefer I make reasonable assumptions and proceed now, I will:
- Assume qualifying accounts are those with Account.Payment_Status__c = 'Good Standing' (or Payment Status = 'Current') and Outstanding_Balance__c = 0.
- Use a standard renewal email/agreement template and send to Account.Primary_Contact_Email__c.
- Update related Opportunity to StageName = 'Contract Sent' and add a task for flagged accounts for Sales review.

Tell me which of the three options above to use (or paste the renewal policy and/or the contract list here) and I’ll proceed immediately.

messages.subject: Renewal Policy Update
messages.body_plain:
Team,

Here is our updated renewal policy:
- Apply a 5% price increase on all renewals
- Only send renewal agreements to accounts in good standing (description must NOT contain 'Problem')
- Flag problem accounts for manual review by creating a Salesforce task
- Update all processed opportunity stages to 'Renewal'

Best,
VP Sales
